_doc: What tool_guard.py lets through. Copy to .claude/hooks/config/tools.json, then check it against the tools your sessions really have: `py .claude/hooks/tool_guard.py --explain Builder <tool name> ...`. A tool of a named server passes only when it's named here. Names take * and ?. Roles are the names in roles.json. A shell command passes only when every pattern it matches allows the session's role, so a pattern for nobody (roles []) is checked whatever else the command holds. Each git pattern is tied to git's own subcommand, after git's options, so a word in a commit message isn't taken for a command.

never.generate_*: we make every asset ourselves, and a generator can cost credits
never.search_asset: it searches the marketplace, and we use no marketplace asset
never.auto_setup_avatar: it builds a rig for us, and our rigs are our own

never.set_session_fast_mode: fast mode is billed at a premium

shell.why: it throws away uncommitted work, and this folder holds every teammate's. Nobody runs it; a blocking file is compared and handled one by one
this folder has one index, so it stages every teammate's files. Stage your own paths by name
it commits every teammate's uncommitted edits as yours. Commit by path
a forced push rewrites what the others already hold. Nobody forces one
a pull, a rebase or a branch switch changes files under every session, and crashes Rojo
who pushes is written in AGENTS.md
it publishes a place from the shell, and publishing is the director's hand
an Open Cloud call from the shell goes round the Open Cloud guard
no session handles the account's cookie
